newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: South Korea to reopen car exports to Taiwan.
newsitem.headline: South Korea to reopen car exports to Taiwan.

text.p: South Korea said on Saturday it would resume vehicle exports to Taiwan which were halted in 1992 after Seoul established diplomatic relations with China.
Seoul's trade ministry said Taiwan agreed to take 7,000 units this year under a quota system, which calls for a 10 percent increase every year.
South Korean vehicle exports have been suspended since August, 1992, when Seoul and Taipei severed diplomatic ties after Seoul normalised ties with Beijing. China views Taiwan as a rebel province.
"We will export our cars to Taiwan again from this year," said Kim Sung-jin, director of the ministry's Asia division.
"Shipment of the 7,000 vehicles would be made in the next two months of so," Kim said.
South Korea exported 8,788 units in the last year preceding the diplomatic row.
Kim said export conditions would improve if Taiwan joins the World Trade Organisation (WTO).
Under the agreement with Taiwan the quota will be raised to 10,000 units in the first year after Taiwan joins the WTO and the number will increase by 20 percent each year.
